Si X ~ N(μ, σ), la variable Z = (X − μ)/: If X ~ N(μ, σ), the variable Z = (X − μ)/σ follows the standard normal N(0, 1), whose distribution function Φ(z) is the one given in the tables. This way any normal probability reduces to Φ: P(X ≤ a) = Φ((a − μ)/σ) and P(X ≥ a) = 1 − Φ((a − μ)/σ). By symmetry, Φ(−z) = 1 − Φ(z).
La binomial B(n, p) cuenta los éxitos en: The binomial B(n, p) counts the successes in n independent trials, each with probability p: mean np and variance npq. The Poisson P(λ) counts rare events in an interval, with mean and variance λ. For discrete distributions it does matter whether the inequality is strict: P(X < k) = P(X ≤ k − 1).
Si np ≥ 5 y nq ≥ 5, la binomial se aprox: If np ≥ 5 and nq ≥ 5, the binomial is approximated by N(np, √(npq)), adding or subtracting 0.5 at the endpoints (continuity correction). If n is large and p is small (n ≥ 30 and p ≤ 0.1), a Poisson with mean λ = np is a better approximation. And a Poisson with λ ≥ 10 is approximated by N(λ, √λ).
La geométrica G(p) cuenta los fracasos a: The geometric G(p) counts the failures before the first success: P(X = k) = q<sup>k</sup>p, with mean q/p. Some books count the trials up to the first success, which is X + 1. The hypergeometric is like the binomial but drawing without replacement: from a population of N elements with K successes, n are drawn, and X counts the successes obtained.
La t de Student con ν grados de libertad: Student's t with ν degrees of freedom appears when estimating a mean using the sample standard deviation: it is symmetric like the normal but with heavier tails, and it resembles the normal as ν grows. The χ² with k degrees of freedom is the sum of k squared standard normals and is used in goodness-of-fit tests, independence tests and for the variance.
La F de Snedecor con d₁ y d₂ grados de l: Snedecor's F with d₁ and d₂ degrees of freedom is the ratio of two χ² each divided by its degrees of freedom. It is used to compare two variances and in analysis of variance. It satisfies F<sub>d₁, d₂; 1−α</sub> = 1/F<sub>d₂, d₁; α</sub>, which is how left-tail values are obtained from the tables.
En la uniforme U(a, b) todos los tramos: In the uniform U(a, b) all stretches of the same length have the same probability: mean (a + b)/2 and variance (b − a)²/12. The exponential with rate λ measures the time until an event; it has mean 1/λ and is memoryless.
Una binomial con np ≥ 5 y nq ≥ 5 se pare: A binomial with np ≥ 5 and nq ≥ 5 resembles the normal N(np, √(npq)), and a Poisson with λ ≥ 10 resembles N(λ, √λ). Since the normal is continuous and the other jumps, each integer k is replaced by the interval from k − 0.5 to k + 0.5: that is the continuity correction. The tool shows side by side the exact probability, the approximation with and without correction, and the error of each. With n ≥ 30 and p ≤ 0.1 the binomial is approximated by a Poisson with λ = np, and a hypergeometric in which less than 10 % of the population is drawn is approximated by a binomial.
Si se toman muestras de n valores de cua: If samples of n values are taken from any distribution with mean μ and standard deviation σ, the mean of each sample has mean μ and standard deviation σ/√n, and as n grows its distribution approaches a normal even if the original one is not. That is why the normal appears in confidence intervals and hypothesis tests. Choose “Central limit theorem” under “What to calculate” to see the histogram of the means of 2000 simulated samples next to the bell curve predicted by the theorem.
Con «Comparar con» se dibuja encima una: “Compare with” draws a second distribution on top, dashed if it is continuous and with dots if it is discrete: it is useful to see how Student's t approaches the normal as the degrees of freedom increase, how a normal changes with its σ, or how well a normal follows a binomial.
Para un nivel de significación α, el val: For a significance level α, the two-tailed critical value c leaves α/2 in each tail: P(−c ≤ Z ≤ c) = 1 − α. With α = 0.05, z<sub>α/2</sub> = 1.96. The one-tailed value leaves all of α in one tail: z<sub>α</sub> = 1.645 for α = 0.05. The χ² and F are not symmetric, so the two-tailed case needs two different values.
Si se sabe una probabilidad, por ejemplo: If a probability is known, for example P(X ≥ a) = p, look up in the table the z with Φ(z) = 1 − p and solve (a − μ)/σ = z for the missing mean or standard deviation.
Para cualquier distribución con media μ: For any distribution with mean μ and standard deviation σ, P(|X − μ| ≤ c) ≥ 1 − σ²/c². It is a bound that always holds, even if the distribution is unknown; for the normal the actual probability is quite a bit higher.
Se tipifica, z = (x − μ)/σ, y se busca e: You standardize, z = (x − μ)/σ, and look up the area up to z. With μ = 100 and σ = 15, P(X < 130) corresponds to z = 2, which gives 0.9772.
